order.why_here: The purest running-state carry: drop a negative prefix and keep one running sum.
Same carry, but a negative flips the order, so the carry holds both the max and the min.
Introduces the reach invariant: the reachable set is a prefix described by one integer.
Reuses the reach, now split into BFS levels that are intervals, to count the minimum jumps.
Converts tap intervals into jump lengths and runs Jump Game II with an impossibility check.
A running sum with restart, justified by an argument that discards whole blocks of starts at once.
Each letter becomes a span; a required end is extended and cut when the sweep catches it.
Constraints from both neighbours, each solved by its own directional greedy pass and combined with max.
Count only the rises: the first of the lower-bound-equals-answer problems.
Two lower bounds (flow across a boundary, surplus at a machine), and the larger one is achievable.
The reach idea returns over subset sums; a forced hole is patched with the hole itself.
Sort by end and place points as far right as possible, an exchange argument applied twice.
Greedy swaps are optimal because the seating decomposes into cycles, counted with union-find.
Greedy that only works with time reversed: peel off the last stamp first.
